1) agouti is a full antagonist for the MC1-R, 2) agouti and alpha-MSH have similar inhibitory effects on the growth of mouse B16-F10 melanoma cells, and 3) the effects of agoutis are not antagonistic but rather additive.
agouti protein is able to inhibit B16 melanoma cell growth and to down-regulate MC1-R expression.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of agouti as an endogenous antagonist of melanogenesis and melanocortin signaling.
the role of agouti protein in melanoma cell growth.
the role of the agouti protein and the melanocortins on the growth of melanoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
agouti is a potent antagonist of alpha-MSR-induced melanogenesis, and an antagonist of the antiproliferation of B16-F10 cells.
agouti protein inhibites growth of B16F1 cells by acting through melanocyte-stimulating receptors, and that this effect is not antagonistic.
agouti protein inhibiting growth of B16 cells is mediated through melanocortiin receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
agouti protein is a dual agonist-antagonist at melanocortin 1 receptors.
agouti inhibits the growth of B-16 melanoma cells by acting via MC1-R but not by antagonizing the effects of alpha-MSI.
agouti is a dual agonist-antagonist of the MC1-R, and that the antiproliferation action is the result of the agonistic action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
agouti is not a simple antagonist of alpha-MSR action in B16-F1 but rather a full agonist of MC1-R.
agouti protein is a potent antiproliferator in melanocytes, and that this effect is independent of its antagonistic effect on cAMP formation.
MC1-R signaling is a complex process, with multiple effects of ligands, and that the melanocortins may have important roles as regulators of cell growth and differentiation.
